notes: Image-alt v1 set: 13 items. Provenance tier: 8 w3c, 5 owner. The w3c-tier items are either a verbatim W3C WAI-tutorial worked-example alt text applied to a substitute image (telephone/fax/print/search icons), or a decorative image, tagged w3c because the ground-truth alt (the empty string) is the universal W3C rule for ALL decorative images regardless of pixel content, not image-specific wording (geometric-pattern, floral-wallpaper, wallpaper-corner). The 5 owner-tier items (a bicycle photograph, three chart/diagram images, and a home icon) carry alt text written for this phase, following the W3C category criteria but not quoting a verbatim W3C example -- that ratio is stated here rather than disguised (D-03). Category counts: informative 4, complex 3, decorative 3, functional 3. Verdict split: 7 issue, 6 pass. Poison items: 4, covering a false-PASS, a false-ISSUE, a filename-as-suggestedAlt plausible-wrong-alt, and an empty-suggestedAlt confident-looking variant -- see each item's poison field. This v1 set covers check: 'alt-text' only. analyse-visual also supports heading-semantics, which needs rendered page screenshots rather than single images and is NOT covered here; this gap is recorded so Phase 84 does not read image-alt.v1.json as covering the whole analyse-visual capability. Licensing: one asset in the set carries an attribution obligation -- img-informative-seed (CC BY 3.0, MichaelMcPhee), inherited from 83-01. Every other asset is CC0 or public domain; see LICENCES.md.
